findings.title: Public findMany method removed, breaking existing callers
findings.body: The service's public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method was deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a raw SQL fragment. Any existing code in the repository that constructs InsightsBookingService and calls `findMany(...)` to fetch bookings will now fail at compile time (or worse, at runtime if untyped) with 'findMany is not a function'. The PR description only mentions test updates, so this removal appears to be an unannounced breaking API change. Either keep `findMany` (implemented via $queryRaw with the base conditions) or update all call sites in the same PR.

findings.title: Caching tests removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous test suite had a 'Caching' describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on second call. These tests were deleted entirely rather than converted to the new Prisma.sql format. The service still contains caching logic (`cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` with the undefined-vs-null distinction), and that logic is now completely untested; a regression in the caching (e.g. caching null filter conditions incorrectly) would go undetected.

findings.title: Tests were never executed; PR author reports test runner failures
findings.body: The PR's own review checklist states 'I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass.' None of the assertions in this file — especially the structural `toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)` comparisons and the `$queryRaw` query against "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" — have been confirmed to pass. Notably, `$queryRaw` in Postgres returns BigInt for bigint columns, so the `expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])` comparison at line 487 will fail if the table's id column is bigint, and the denormalized table must be populated (e.g. by trigger) for the booking created via `prisma.booking.create` for the row to appear at all. These tests must be run and confirmed green before merging.

findings.title: Array parameters passed to ANY() rely on Prisma raw array serialization
findings.body: The org- and team-scope conditions pass plain JavaScript arrays as raw query parameters, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))\``. Whether this works depends on how the Prisma query engine serializes JS arrays for raw queries; the established, safe pattern is `${Prisma.join(teamIds)}` inside an `IN (...)` clause. If serialization sends the array as a JSON/text parameter rather than a Postgres array, `= ANY(...)` will throw a type error at query time — and since the PR author could not run the tests, this has not been verified. Verify `ANY(${array})` executes correctly against Postgres, or switch to `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})`.
